ogis draws maps on [MapLibre](https://maplibre.org) from data that stay in DuckDB: a parquet file, a lazy
table, a data frame or an sf object. A map is built with the pipe, a layer at a time, and every map below is live:
pan it, zoom it, click a point.

## A first map

The example data are the positions of four vessels on the Icelandic groundfish survey in March 2019, one row a
position, with whether a tow was on.

```{r}
library(ogis)
positions <- og_example("trawlsurvey")
positions |> og_point(colour = behaviour)
```

`colour` takes a column written bare. Its values get a colour each and a legend; the map opens on the rows' extent.

## Layers with the pipe

`og_map()` starts a map from data, and each layer function adds a layer over the ones before. Here a line per vessel
in the order of time, and the positions over it: two columns to colour by (the first shown; the other is a choice in
the page), and a click that shows the row.

```{r}
og_map(positions) |>
  og_path(group = vid, time = time, name = "Tracks") |>
  og_point(
    colour = c(behaviour, speed),
    popup = c(vid, time, speed, behaviour),
    name = "Positions"
  )
```

`og_map()` with no data starts a map whose layers bring their own. The survey's tows are lines, one a row:

```{r}
#| out-height: 400px
og_map() |>
  og_line(og_example("trawlsurveytows"), name = "Tows") |>
  og_point(positions, colour = behaviour, name = "Positions",
           visible = FALSE)
```

`visible = FALSE` leaves a layer off when the page opens; its box in the sidebar turns it on.

## Rings and outlines

`stroke` draws each point as a ring of its colour, `stroke` pixels wide, hollow, `size` across; `fill = NA` an area's
outline alone. A click inside either still shows its row. Here the positions faster than 12 knots ringed over the
others:

```{r}
fast <- dplyr::filter(positions, speed > 12)
og_map(positions) |>
  og_point(colour = behaviour, name = "Positions") |>
  og_point(fast, colour = "#00a5c8", size = 14, stroke = 2,
           name = "Over 12 knots")
```

## In MapLibre's own terms

Every layer function takes MapLibre's paint and layout properties by their own names, in quotes, for what its own
arguments do not reach; and `id`, the name a page's address and a script know the layer by. Here the tows dashed:

```{r}
#| out-height: 400px
og_map() |>
  og_line(og_example("trawlsurveytows"), colour = "#4a5560", name = "Tows",
          "line-dasharray" = list(2, 1))
```

## The order of layers

Each layer is drawn over the ones before it, whatever box of the sidebar it sits in (`section`). `order` in `og_map()`
draws the layers it names first, by their `id`, under the others; the sidebar keeps its own order. Here the tows,
listed last under *Reference*, drawn under the positions:

```{r}
og_map(positions, order = "tows") |>
  og_point(colour = behaviour, name = "Positions") |>
  og_line(og_example("trawlsurveytows"), colour = "#4a5560", id = "tows",
          name = "Tows", section = "Reference")
```

## Finding a row

`search` names a column whose values the page's *Find* box, above the sidebar's boxes, looks through: whole matches
first, then values that begin with what is typed, then any that hold it, case and accents aside, each kind nearest the
view's centre first. A click on one takes the map there and shows its row. Here the tows by their id; type `4906`:

```{r}
#| out-height: 400px
og_map() |>
  og_line(og_example("trawlsurveytows"), popup = id.lgs, search = id.lgs,
          name = "Tows")
```

## The sea floor

`og_relief()` draws a depth model's depth in colour and its relief shaded; `og_contour()` the lines of equal depth,
the charts' depths a little heavier and labelled, thinner lines between. Here the Danish waters' depths, made into
tiles once by `og_tiles_dem()` and given to both, under the harbours:

```{r}
depth <- og_tiles_dem(og_example("dansk_relief"), maxzoom = 6)
og_map(view = list(bounds = c(2.5, 54.5, 13, 58.5))) |>
  og_relief(depth) |>
  og_contour(depth) |>
  og_polygon(og_example("dansk_harbours"), fill = NA, colour = "#b2182b",
             name = "Harbours")
```

The arguments are where the map starts; the page's controls, folded under ▸ beside each layer's name, change the
colours, the shading and the lines. The depth is grey at 75 % by default, quiet under the map's own data; a map whose
subject is the sea floor might start otherwise:

```{r}
#| eval: false
og_relief(depth, palette = "seabed", opacity = 100, limits = c(5, 60), shade = 0.8)
og_contour(depth, major = c(10, 20, 30, 50), minor = FALSE)
```

A depth model kept as an MBTiles file in its own place on each computer can be named once there, by a line in
`.Renviron` (`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it), so a script shared between colleagues carries no path:

```
OGIS_DEPTH=D:/data/depth.mbtiles
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
og_map() |> og_relief() |> og_contour() # the model OGIS_DEPTH names
```

## A layer of your own

What the layer functions do not draw, an `og_layer()` does, in MapLibre's own terms: a style of your own on
elevations, contours or tiles of your own. `og_add_layer()` puts one into the pipe, in a box of the sidebar of its own.
Here the Danish depths again, in colour by a layer written out in full, as `og_relief()` writes it:

```{r}
own <- og_layer(
  "depth", "dem", label = "Depth",
  tiles = og_tiles_dem(og_example("dansk_relief"), maxzoom = 6),
  style = list(list(id = "depth-colour", type = "color-relief")),
  colour = list(palette = "seabed", opacity = 75)
)
og_map(view = list(bounds = c(2.5, 54.5, 13, 58.5))) |>
  og_add_layer(own, section = "Sea floor") |>
  og_polygon(og_example("dansk_harbours"), fill = NA, colour = "#b2182b",
             name = "Harbours")
```

The harbours, their outlines alone, reach from Greenland to the Black Sea, so `view` opens the map on the grid's box.
Elevations and contours go under the base map's place names, whatever their order in the pipe; the box *Depth* has the
colours' controls.

## A base map of your own

A base map is a MapLibre style, or a picture's tiles by address: by zoom and place (`{z}/{x}/{y}`), or a WMS's
`GetMap` with each tile's box (`{bbox-epsg-3857}`). The first given is the one the map opens on, the others choices
under *Base map*. Here GEBCO's shaded sea floor from its WMS, which reaches past Europe's seas, then ogis's own:

```{r}
gebco <- list(
  id = "gebco", label = "Sea floor (GEBCO)",
  attribution = "Imagery reproduced from the GEBCO Grid, GEBCO Compilation Group",
  tiles = paste0(
    "https://wms.gebco.net/mapserv?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0&REQUEST=GetMap",
    "&LAYERS=GEBCO_LATEST&STYLES=&FORMAT=image/png&CRS=EPSG:3857",
    "&WIDTH=256&HEIGHT=256&BBOX={bbox-epsg-3857}"
  )
)
og_map(positions, basemaps = c(list(gebco), og_basemaps())) |>
  og_point(colour = behaviour, name = "Positions")
```

A picture alone has no place names, and the layers' texts are drawn in the browser's own font. `labels`, a style's
address, puts that style's names over it with its fonts, as on `og_basemaps()`'s, which take Carto's.

## Showing and sharing

- **In R**, printing a map serves it on this computer and opens it in RStudio's Viewer or a browser.
- **In a document** (Quarto, R Markdown, a pkgdown article like this one), a printed map is drawn live in the page.
- **As a folder**, `og_bundle(map, "my-map")` writes the map with its data, to open with a double click on any
  computer, with no R and no server.
